To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
gappy alignments derived from partial genes are problematic for phylogenetic inference, and that alignment masking is a useful tool for reducing the effect of the gappiness.

(1) the pattern of gappiness in multiple sequence alignments can have a dramatic impact on phylogenetic accuracy, even in the absence alignment error, and (2) the use of alignment subdivision and alignment masking can improve phylogenetic accuracy.

1) Gappy multiple sequence alignments, which are common in phylogenomics, can lead to substantial errors in phylogenetic inference.2) The error in phylogenetic analysis from gappy alignments is beyond what would be predicted from the amount of missing information in the alignment.3) The error can be substantially reduced by either masking or subdividing the alignment.
